Attribution is strict, each guard a rule and not a special case: a quantity attributes only when the text introducing it (the thirty-two characters before it, plus a table cell's row label and column header) carries a token distinctive to the item - the item's own tokens minus its same-dimension siblings', the siblings found in keys.json by the item's (name, value) pair - and no token distinctive to a rival sibling; function words never attribute; a heading is a section delimiter, not a per-quantity label; a quantity inside parentheses is an aside or a reference the label carries; LaTeX '{,}' digit grouping and the inline-math delimiters are normalized away; and a quantity introduced by a bound word (max, minimum, threshold, limit, peak, upper, lower, bound) states a requirement, not the item's value, so it attributes to no item unless the item's own name carries the bound word.
